description: Reorganize the issue detail page from a flat stack of same-weight cards into three attention-graded tiers: a sticky status headline (heaviest), an attention-ordered reading flow (medium), and a metadata/reference rail (lightest). Web-only layout reorganization; no server/runner/CLI/API changes.

tasks.title: Three-tier layout shell + sticky StatusHeadline + single-runtime-badge invariant
tasks.description: Introduce the three-tier layout shell in IssueDetailPage.tsx (status-header region, reading-flow column at lg:col-span-2, reference-rail column at lg:col-span-1) and reassign every existing block to its target tier per the design D2 table — blocks are moved, not rewritten. Introduce a new sticky StatusHeadline presentation component that aggregates decision.summary (icon + tone), the current stage name + completed/total progress from workflowStageProgress, and decision.currentTask.title into one pinned region (sticky top-0 z-20, data-sticky="true"), reusing the runtimeSummaryPresentation tone map for the semantic fill. Apply D5 to resolve duplicate runtime state: the identity row keeps exactly one RuntimeSummaryPill, and RuntimeDecisionSurface drops its own summary label/icon row (defers to the headline) while remaining anchored in the status-header tier directly beneath the headline (non-sticky). Remove the standalone "Workflow Interrupted" card (subsumed by deriveRuntimeDecision's blocked rationale shown in the headline). Update the existing IssueDetailPage.{main,readiness,capacity-gating,archived}.test.tsx suites in place to the new tier anchors and ordering, and add status-header spec coverage.
acceptanceCriteria: IssueDetailPage renders three tier containers with stable anchors (data-testid for status-header-tier, reading-flow, reference-rail) and a status-headline anchor
StatusHeadline is the only sticky element: its className contains 'sticky', it carries data-sticky="true", and it is the first child of the scroll container (issue-detail-page-container)

When situation + stage + progress + current task are all available, the headline displays them together in one region; when no stage/progress exists (backlog) it shows the situation alone without fabricating a figure; for archived done it reflects done with no active workflow controls
The headline reflects exactly one adjudicated situation (running / queued / approval-required / blocked / failed / done) sourced from deriveRuntimeDecision
The identity row renders exactly one runtime-status-pill; RuntimeDecisionSurface no longer renders its own summary label/icon row (no duplicate same-weight indicator)
RuntimeDecisionSurface (all 7 runtime actions: approve/send-back/stop/start/retry/resume/rerun) renders within the status-header tier, not in the reading flow or the reference rail
The standalone "Workflow Interrupted" card is removed; interrupted health is surfaced via the reducer's blocked rationale in the headline/surface

Existing IssueDetailPage.main.test.tsx, IssueDetailPage.readiness.test.tsx, IssueDetailPage.capacity-gating.test.tsx, IssueDetailPage.archived.test.tsx are updated to the new anchors/ordering and pass (no old+new duplication)

New spec tests cover: stickiness (data-sticky + className + first-child), single glanceable region, adjudicated situation variants (running/approval-required/done-archived), stage+progress display, current task title, action-surface anchoring in header tier, single-badge count invariant, and heaviest visual weight (sticky+fill+icon+border combination unique to the header)
npm run typecheck -w packages/web passes with no warnings-as-errors
tasks.output: packages/web/src/pages/issue-detail/ui/IssueDetailPage.tsx (restructured), new StatusHeadline component, updated IssueDetailPage.*.test.tsx suites, new status-header spec tests
tasks.notes: This is the foundational structural task: the D2 block reassignment is atomic, so all blocks move here even though later tasks refine per-tier chrome. Reuse every block component unchanged (reposition, not rewrite). StatusHeadline consumes existing projections verbatim (deriveRuntimeDecision, workflowStageProgress) — no new data/state. Confirm the scroll container is issue-detail-page-container and set top-0 relative to it.

tasks.title: Reading flow — lightest chrome, collapsible key-signal, and attention ordering
tasks.description: Refine the reading-flow tier (whose blocks are already placed by T-001) to honor the reading-flow spec: apply content-forward, lightest chrome (drop heavy CardSection borders/fills for purely-content blocks like description and comments; keep minimal treatment for structured summaries so flow chrome is never heavier than rail items), and ensure collapsible long blocks — IssueDescriptionSection and IssueDiffFilesSection — preserve a key signal when collapsed (description presence + leading text hint; file/addition/deletion counts). Add reading-flow spec tests asserting the attention ordering, maximum-width column, lightest-chrome weight, medium tier weight, collapsible-signal preservation, and exclusion of the decision surface and rail content from the flow.
acceptanceCriteria: Reading-flow content blocks do not carry heavier card chrome than reference-rail items; purely-content blocks (description, comments) present content directly without heavy bordered/filled card wrappers
A collapsed long description still shows a signal that it exists plus a hint of its content (does not vanish from the flow)
A collapsed change/diff list still shows the file, addition, and deletion counts so the scale of the change remains visible
Tests assert the attention ordering via compareDocumentPosition: workflow progress/outputs precede changes/diff, which precede commits, which precede description, which precedes comments
Tests assert the reading-flow column is the maximum-width body column (lg:col-span-2 of lg:grid-cols-3, wider than the rail)
Tests assert the runtime decision/action surface and the metadata/model/workflow-profile/prerequisites/drift/convergence blocks are not placed inside the reading flow
Tests assert the reading-flow tier is visually lighter than the status headline and heavier than the reference rail (medium weight)
npm run typecheck -w packages/web and npm run test:run -w packages/web pass
tasks.output: Updated reading-flow block chrome in IssueDetailPage.tsx and section components, collapsible key-signal behavior, new reading-flow spec tests
tasks.notes: Block placement/ordering is established by T-001; this task owns the presentation weight and collapsibility rules. Final per-block chrome is settled against the 'lighter than rail' spec assertion (design D6). Keep min-w-0 overflow handling intact (relied on by repository-metadata containment tests).

tasks.title: Reference rail — desktop right column, narrow-screen collapse, default-collapsed low-frequency items
tasks.description: Refine the reference-rail tier (whose blocks are already placed by T-001) to honor the reference-rail spec: confirm the desktop right column (lg:col-span-1) is narrower than the reading flow; on narrow screens render the rail as stacked collapsible sections beneath the reading flow (no right column, no drawer — drawer is a mobile affordance scoped to the next issue); default-collapse the low-frequency drift and convergence panels (data-collapsed="true", expand on demand); keep rail cards on the CardSection substrate with muted tokens so they carry the lightest visual weight. Add reference-rail spec tests asserting metadata/config-only content, desktop right-column layout, narrow-screen collapse, default-collapse + expand-on-demand, lightest weight, and exclusion of primary content.
acceptanceCriteria: The reference rail holds only metadata and low-frequency configuration (details, model, workflow-profile control, prerequisites, drift, convergence) plus IssueActionsCard; it does not contain the decision/action surface, workflow progress/outputs, changes/diff, commits, description, or comments
On desktop the rail renders as a right column beside the reading flow, narrower than the reading-flow column
On a narrow viewport the rail renders as stacked collapsed sections and does not occupy a right column beside the reading flow
The drift panel is collapsed by default (data-collapsed="true" / body absent) and expands only on a deliberate user click
The convergence panel is collapsed by default and expands only on a deliberate user click
Rail cards keep the CardSection substrate and muted tokens so the rail is visually lighter than the reading flow (lightest tier)
Tests assert each of the above scenarios from the reference-rail spec
npm run typecheck -w packages/web and npm run test:run -w packages/web pass
tasks.output: Updated reference-rail rendering in IssueDetailPage.tsx (narrow-screen collapse, default-collapse state), new reference-rail spec tests
tasks.notes: The desktop right column grid is established by T-001; this task owns the narrow-screen fallback rendering and the default-collapse behavior for drift/convergence. Do not implement a drawer/bottom-sheet (explicitly scoped to the next issue).

tasks.title: Cross-tier verification of all conditional paths + full typecheck/test green
tasks.description: Perform a holistic cross-tier verification pass spanning all three tiers, which the per-tier tasks (T-001..T-003) cannot fully cover in isolation. Walk every conditional path the detail page supports — archived, backlog/readiness, draft, base drift, convergence items, interrupted health, PR delivery, and capacity gating — and verify each renders its blocks in the correct assigned tier with correct anchors, that no block is lost, duplicated, or orphaned across tiers, and that the three-tier visual weight hierarchy (status headline heaviest > reading flow > reference rail lightest) holds across every path. Run the full web typecheck and test suite green as the final gate.
acceptanceCriteria: Every conditional path (archived, backlog/readiness, draft, drift, convergence, interrupted health, PR delivery, capacity gating) renders its blocks in the tier assigned by design D2 with the expected anchors
No block is lost, duplicated, or rendered in more than one tier across any conditional path

The three-tier visual weight hierarchy holds for each conditional path: status headline (sticky + fill + icon + border) > reading flow (widest, calm chrome) > reference rail (narrow, muted, partly collapsed)
The archived and capacity-gating test suites (the designated regression sentinels) pass
npm run typecheck -w packages/web passes with no warnings-as-errors
npm run test:run -w packages/web passes in full (all suites green, no skipped tests masking flakiness)
tasks.output: Verification report (per conditional path -> tier assignment -> pass/fail) and a green full web typecheck + test run
tasks.notes: This is the cross-tier integration gate; the #1 design risk is a layout reshuffle regressing a conditional path. Reuse of unchanged block components is the primary mitigation — verify no block internals were accidentally rewritten. If the reducer's blocked wording proves insufficient for interrupted health (Open Question), restore the removed card as a collapsed rail item rather than re-introducing it in the flow.
